[USER] User struggles with maintaining consistent positive self-talk.  
[USER] User tends to beat themselves up when they slip up.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Common negative self-talk examples include: "I'm not good enough," "I'm too [fill in the blank]," "I don't deserve good things," "I always mess things up," and "I'm not lovable."  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] To reframe "I'm not good enough," say "I am capable and worthy, and I will continue to learn and grow."  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] To reframe "I'm too [fill in the blank]," say "I may be [fill in the blank], but that does not determine my worth or ability to love and care for myself."  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] To reframe "I don't deserve good things," say "I am deserving of love, happiness, and all the good things life has to offer."  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] To reframe "I always mess things up," say "It's okay to make mistakes, and I will continue to learn and grow from them."  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] To reframe "I'm not lovable," say "I am worthy of love and affection, and my flaws do not define my worth as a person."  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggestions to catch and stop negative self-talk include: practicing mindfulness, challenging negative self-talk, reframing negative self-talk, being kind to oneself, and surrounding oneself with positivity.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] To make positive self-talk a habit, create a list of positive affirmations, replace negative thoughts with positive ones, practice gratitude, surround oneself with positivity, and celebrate small victories.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Tips for maintaining consistent positive self-talk include practicing self-compassion, focusing on progress not perfection, finding supportive people, using visualization techniques, practicing self-care, and staying mindful.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Strategies for practicing self-compassion in the moment include: speaking kindly to oneself, acknowledging feelings, reminding oneself that everyone makes mistakes, taking a break, remembering strengths, and connecting with others.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Self-compassion involves acknowledging effort and progress towards positive self-talk.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Self-care activities can include taking a walk, meditating, or doing something enjoyable.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Practicing self-compassion takes time and is about developing a mindset of kindness, understanding, and self-acceptance.
